ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure marks the “horizon”; the sun is located near the horizon; a straight railway extends into the distance, and the sun appears to be setting exactly between the extension lines of the two rails. Reasoning: The key to this scene is not that the railway itself moves, but that the fixed direction of the railway is consistent with the sunset azimuth of that day. The location in the question is fixed on the North China Plain, and the direction of the railway is also fixed, so if the same scene appears on another date, the sunset azimuth should be the same as that on May 1, 2012. At the same location, the sunset azimuth is mainly determined by the solar declination, so the other date should be a date when the solar declination is approximately the same as that on May 1. May 1 is before the summer solstice, and the solar declination is a positive value in the Northern Hemisphere; after the summer solstice, the solar declination will again decrease to the same value. Checking the solar declination in 2012 or estimating with the solar declination formula, the date after the summer solstice with a declination close to that of May 1 is approximately August 14, 2012.
